preamble: Nasalization of [i] accompanied by lowering to close-mid [ẽ]. In the Swabian dialect of Horb, as recorded by Kauffmann (1890) and analysed by Kniess (2025), Middle High German short i before a nasal consonant became nasalized and lowered to [ẽ] (Kniess's diachronic Nasal Lowering), so MHG sind, linde and hinder are Horb [sẽntʰ], [lẽntʰ] and [hẽnd̥r]. The lowering merged these words with old e before a nasal (MHG hende 'hands' [hẽntʰ]); Kniess analyses the modern forms as having underlying /e/, which Regressive Nasalization still nasalizes synchronically.

examples.note: Kniess (2025, §5.8) gives the modern underlying form as /hend̥r/, merged with the vowel of MHG hende 'hands' [hẽntʰ].

sources: Kniess, T. B. (2025). Nasalization and Nasal Vowels in the Swabian Dialect of Horb: A Phonological Analysis of Kauffmann 1890. PhD dissertation, Indiana University. https://scholarworks.iu.edu/dspace/items/f9ca887d-4125-46c1-8eb0-933b17f7d00c
